findings.detail: The removed line was `model: "gemini-3-pro-preview"` with the comment "Switched to PRO for better reasoning on data analysis tasks" — an explicit, documented model choice. The replacement passes `'fast'`, and `MODEL_CANDIDATES.fast` leads with `gemini-3.1-flash`, `gemini-3-flash`, `gemini-3-flash-preview` before it ever reaches a Pro id (services/geminiService.ts:43-49). So the *normal* path for this feature is now Flash, not Pro. That is a change in output quality for the one feature in the app that asks the model to reason over a spreadsheet and emit a runnable Python script — exactly the workload the earlier comment said needed Pro. The fallback fix (the actual point of this PR) is orthogonal to the tier and does not require it: `generateText(prompt, 'quality')` gets the same candidate walk with the intended model. The inline comment says "'fast' by request", which is a claim a reviewer cannot verify from the diff; if the downgrade was intentional, the reason belongs in the commit body next to the decision it reverses. Kept at medium rather than high because output is still produced and the revert is one argument.
findings.summary: Data-analyst call moved from Pro to the Flash-leading 'fast' tier

findings.detail: The SDK mock returns `{ text: 'ok' }` (line 25). `translateBatch` does `JSON.parse(response.text || "[]")` (services/geminiService.ts:295), and `'ok'` is not valid JSON, so every one of the four `translateBatch` tests lands in the `catch` at line 297 and receives `items.map(() => "")` — i.e. `['']`. The notice assertions still hold (the fallback happens before the parse), so three of the tests are fine by accident. The fourth is not: `it('still translates when the caller passes no handler')` at line 225 asserts only `.resolves.toBeDefined()` (line 231), and `['']` is defined. The test therefore passes on a run that translated nothing — which is precisely the silent-blank failure mode commits 4c9f7f5 and 0cb84be exist to eliminate, and the one the new TranslateTab guard at components/TranslateTab.tsx:319-330 is written to catch. A false-green here is the same shape the PR calls out in its own comments. No user impact, hence low.
findings.summary: All four translateBatch tests run through the JSON-parse failure path

findings.detail: Below the code-smells handbook's duplication threshold (one new site, ~12 lines, not 15+ in 2+ places), so this is an observation rather than a finding. `generateText` (465-486) is a character-for-character copy of the `for (;;) { try … catch { retireModel } }` block in `processGeneralFile` (438-452) — the author's own doc comment says "Same shape as `processGeneralFile`'s loop". With `verifyGeminiKey` now carrying a third, deliberately different variant (it walks but must not record), the retire-and-advance policy lives in several places and a future change to it — say, logging the walk or capping it — has to be made in each.
findings.summary: generateText duplicates processGeneralFile's retire-and-advance loop verbatim

findings.detail: Observation on a design choice this PR makes, not a request. `translateBatch`'s signature promises `Promise<string[]>`, while line 295 returns whatever `JSON.parse` produced — an object, a number, a nested array, or a short array are all possible from a model reply. This PR correctly defends against that, but it does so in the *caller* (components/TranslateTab.tsx:328-330 checks `Array.isArray` and length), so the type still lies at the boundary and any future caller inherits the hazard without the guard. `TranslateTab` is the only caller today, so nothing is broken. Noting it because the guard's own comment identifies the parse as the root cause, and the cheaper long-term home for that check is inside the function whose return type makes the promise.
findings.summary: translateBatch is typed string[] but returns unvalidated JSON.parse output
